questions.question: What is the default administrative access port for FortiGate HTTPS management?
questions.explanation: FortiGate HTTPS management uses port 443 by default. HTTP uses port 80. Both can be changed in the interface settings under System > Network > Interfaces.

questions.question: Which FortiGate operating mode provides the most transparent deployment with no IP addressing required on the unit itself?
questions.explanation: Transparent mode deploys FortiGate as a Layer 2 bridge — no IP addresses needed on the physical interfaces. All traffic passes through transparently, making it ideal for inserting security into existing networks without redesign.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate security policy and what components does it require at minimum?
options: Incoming interface, outgoing interface, source, destination, and action (ACCEPT/DENY) — these five elements define a policy match
questions.explanation: FortiGate security policies require: Incoming Interface, Outgoing Interface, Source (address/user/internet service), Destination, and Action. Schedule, services (ports), and security profiles are additional optional components.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's NGFW mode and how does it differ from profile-based mode?
options: NGFW mode: application and user-based policies with application control and IPS directly in the policy (no separate profile). Profile-based: security profiles (AV, web filter, IPS) attached separately to policies — profile-based supports more features
questions.explanation: Profile-based (default): flexible, attach multiple profiles. NGFW mode: streamlined, policy-level application and user control, no separate AV/web-filter profiles in policy. NGFW mode requires proxy inspection. Choose based on deployment needs.

questions.question: What is FortiGuard and what services does it provide?
options: Fortinet's threat intelligence and subscription service providing: antivirus signatures, web filtering category ratings, IPS signatures, application signatures, IP reputation, botnet C&C blocking, and spam filtering — all updated from Fortinet's global threat research
questions.explanation: FortiGuard services: AV (virus/malware signatures), Web Filter (URL categories), IPS (vulnerability exploit signatures), Application Control (application signatures), Anti-Spam, DNS Filter, Industrial Security, OT security signatures. Updated multiple times daily.

questions.question: What is the difference between flow-based and proxy-based inspection on FortiGate?
options: Flow-based: fast, one-pass packet inspection with minimal latency, limited deep inspection capabilities. Proxy-based: full content buffering and reassembly, deeper inspection (certificates, file content), higher latency, more CPU/memory
questions.explanation: Flow-based: stream-based scanning, fast, lower resource usage. Good for high-throughput. Proxy-based: buffers entire content, enables: certificate inspection, DLP, antivirus on compressed files, advanced URL filtering. Default varies by model and policy type.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SSL/TLS inspection and what are its two modes?
options: SSL Inspection: decrypts TLS traffic to inspect content. Two modes: (1) Certificate Inspection — only checks server certificate validity (no content decryption). (2) Full SSL Inspection — decrypts, inspects, re-encrypts traffic. Requires trusted CA certificate on clients
questions.explanation: Full SSL inspection: FortiGate acts as man-in-the-middle. Clients must trust FortiGate's signing CA (push via group policy). Certificate inspection: faster, no decryption, only validates certificates. Deep inspection is required for AV, web filtering, IPS to see inside HTTPS.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate Virtual IP (VIP) and what does it do?
options: Maps an external IP address to an internal server (destination NAT/port forwarding) — incoming traffic destined for the external IP is translated to the internal server's IP. Supports IP mapping and port forwarding
questions.explanation: VIP: destination NAT. Map external IP (published) to internal server (real IP). Can also do port mapping (e.g., external TCP/443 → internal TCP/8443). VIP must be used as destination in security policy to allow the inbound traffic after translation.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's VDOM (Virtual Domain) feature?
options: Divides one physical FortiGate into multiple independent virtual firewalls — each VDOM has its own interfaces, routing, policies, and VPN. Management VDOM handles admin access. Uses: multi-tenant environments, separating security domains
questions.explanation: VDOMs: virtual firewall partitioning. Root VDOM (management). Additional VDOMs for tenant separation. Inter-VDOM links connect VDOMs internally. VDOM admin can only manage their VDOM. Requires VDOM license for more than 10 VDOMs. Supported on most FortiGate models.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's HA (High Availability) clustering modes?
options: Active-Passive (A-P): one unit active, one standby — instant failover, simple. Active-Active (A-A): both units process traffic via load balancing — higher throughput, complex session sync. Both use FGCP protocol over heartbeat interfaces
questions.explanation: HA with FGCP (FortiGate Clustering Protocol): A-P for simplicity, A-A for performance. Requirements: same FortiGate model, same firmware, direct heartbeat link. Sync: configuration, session tables, routing tables, firewall policies. Election: primary unit based on priority + serial number.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate SD-WAN feature?
options: Software-Defined WAN: intelligently routes traffic across multiple WAN links based on performance metrics (latency, jitter, packet loss) and application requirements — provides link failover, load balancing, and SLA-based path selection
questions.explanation: FortiGate SD-WAN: define WAN members (ISP1, ISP2, MPLS). SD-WAN rules route specific applications (VoIP, Office 365) to best-performing link. Performance SLA monitors link quality. Load balancing: spillover, round-robin, weighted. Replaces policy-based routing for multi-WAN.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Application Control and what can it identify?
options: Identifies and controls thousands of applications by traffic patterns, signatures, and behavior — regardless of port or protocol. Can allow/block specific apps, limit bandwidth, and report usage. Uses FortiGuard App Control signatures
questions.explanation: App Control: identify applications by layer 7 signatures (Facebook, Netflix, BitTorrent, custom apps). Actions: allow, block, monitor, shape (rate limit). Works even when apps use non-standard ports or HTTPS. Requires flow or proxy inspection. Updated via FortiGuard.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) and what does it protect against?
options: Inspects traffic for known exploit attempts, vulnerability scans, and attack patterns — blocks intrusions using FortiGuard IPS signatures. Protects against: buffer overflows, SQL injection, XSS, exploit kits, brute force, DoS attacks
questions.explanation: FortiGate IPS: signature-based + anomaly-based detection. Signatures from FortiGuard IPS service. Detect and block: known CVE exploits, protocol anomalies, botnet traffic, DoS. Can run in flow or proxy mode. Tuning: disable noisy signatures, create exceptions for false positives.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate address object and what types exist?
options: Named objects representing IP addresses used in policies: Subnet (IP/mask), IP Range, FQDN (resolves DNS dynamically), Geography (country-based), Wildcard FQDN (*.domain.com), Address Group (multiple addresses)
questions.explanation: Address types: Subnet (192.168.1.0/24), IP Range (192.168.1.1-192.168.1.10), FQDN (resolves to IP via DNS), Geography (block/allow by country), Wildcard FQDN (*.microsoft.com), MAC address. Address Groups aggregate multiple objects for policy simplification.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Web Filtering feature?
options: Controls web access by URL category, URL reputation, and specific URLs. FortiGuard provides 75+ categories (Adult, Social Media, Shopping, etc.). Can override ratings, apply quotas, and show block pages. Supports both DNS-based and HTTP/HTTPS inspection
questions.explanation: Web Filtering: FortiGuard URL categories + custom URL lists. Flow-based: category filtering only. Proxy-based: URL + keyword filtering, content rating, safe search enforcement. FortiGuard rating database updated continuously. Per-policy profiles allow different rules for different user groups.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Antivirus and how does it scan traffic?
options: Scans file transfers (HTTP/S downloads, email, FTP, SMB) for malware using FortiGuard AV signatures, heuristic analysis, and optionally cloud-based scanning. Flow-based: scan during transmission. Proxy-based: buffer entire file before allowing download
questions.explanation: AV scanning modes: flow-based (partial buffering, fast, may miss some) vs proxy-based (full file buffer, thorough, more latency). FortiGuard: signature updates + AI/ML detection + cloud sandbox integration. Scans: HTTP, HTTPS (with SSL inspection), FTP, SMTP, POP3, IMAP, SMB.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate IPsec VPN tunnel mode vs dial-up mode?
options: Tunnel mode: site-to-site VPN with static peers (both endpoints have known IPs). Dial-up mode: hub accepts connections from multiple remote sites/clients with dynamic IPs — hub has static IP, spokes dial in
questions.explanation: Site-to-Site tunnel: both FortiGates configured as peers. Dial-up: hub FortiGate has template for accepting multiple unknown-IP peers. Dial-up required for FortiClient remote access VPN or branch offices with dynamic IPs. Phase 1 + Phase 2 negotiation for both modes.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SSL-VPN and how does it differ from IPsec VPN?
options: SSL-VPN: clientless (web browser portal) or client-based (FortiClient tunnel) using TLS. Works through most firewalls/NAT. IPsec: requires UDP/500, 4500 and ESP protocol — may be blocked by some firewalls. SSL-VPN: easier for remote users, web portal for clientless access
questions.explanation: SSL-VPN advantages: easier traversal through NAT/firewalls (uses HTTPS/443), web portal for clientless access to internal web apps, split tunneling configurable. IPsec advantages: better performance, full network access, better for site-to-site. FortiClient supports both.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's user authentication integration with Active Directory?
options: LDAP integration queries Active Directory for user/group membership — used in policies for user-based access control. FortiAuthenticator or RADIUS can also bridge AD authentication. Kerberos or FSSO (Fortinet SSO) provides transparent authentication
questions.explanation: AD integration methods: (1) LDAP: query AD for group membership, user must authenticate to FortiGate. (2) FSSO (Fortinet Single Sign-On): agent on Windows DC monitors logon events → sends IP-to-user mappings to FortiGate — transparent, no re-authentication. (3) RADIUS with AD backend.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Central NAT Table (CNT)?
options: Centralized NAT configuration that separates NAT rules from security policies — define source NAT (SNAT) and destination NAT (DNAT) rules independently from security policy, providing better visibility and management of NAT rules
questions.explanation: Central NAT: enable in System > Feature Visibility. NAT is defined in separate Central SNAT (source NAT rules) and VIP (destination NAT) tables rather than inline in security policies. Provides: better NAT visibility, easier auditing, consistent NAT behavior. Requires policy redesign when enabling.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's ADVPN (Auto Discovery VPN)?
options: Enables spoke-to-spoke VPN tunnels to be established on-demand without going through the hub — spokes discover each other's IP via the hub and create direct shortcuts. Reduces latency for inter-spoke traffic
questions.explanation: ADVPN: hub-and-spoke IPSEC with dynamic spoke-to-spoke shortcuts. When spoke A communicates with spoke B, the hub signals both to establish a direct shortcut tunnel. Traffic bypasses hub once shortcut is up. Requires IBGP or OSPF over VPN for dynamic routing. Great for SD-WAN over VPN.

questions.question: What command shows the routing table on FortiGate?
questions.explanation: 'get router info routing-table all': displays all routes (connected, static, dynamic). 'get router info routing-table database': shows full RIB including inactive routes. 'get router info bgp network': BGP routes. 'diagnose ip route list': kernel routing table. CLI accessed via SSH or console.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's DNS Filter feature?
options: Blocks malicious domain names at DNS resolution time — before any connection is established. FortiGuard DNS categories (botnet, phishing, malware C&C) block DNS queries for known malicious domains. Faster blocking than URL filtering
questions.explanation: DNS Filter: intercepts DNS queries, checks against FortiGuard DNS reputation database. Block: malware, botnet C&C, phishing domains before connection. Safe search enforcement: force SafeSearch on Google/Bing. DNS over HTTPS (DoH) handling. Complements URL filtering with faster, earlier blocking.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's traffic shaping and what can it control?
options: Manages bandwidth allocation per policy, application, or user: guaranteed bandwidth (minimum), maximum bandwidth (ceiling), and traffic priority (DSCP marking). Shared shapers apply across all matching traffic
questions.explanation: Traffic Shaping: per-IP, shared, or per-policy shapers. Guaranteed bandwidth: reserved minimum. Maximum bandwidth: hard ceiling. Priority queues: ensure critical traffic (VoIP) gets forwarded before bulk transfers. Can apply DSCP marking for QoS enforcement downstream.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate packet flow order for incoming traffic?
options: Ingress: (1) Ingress NIC → (2) DoS policy → (3) IPsec decryption → (4) IP integrity check → (5) Routing → (6) DNAT (VIP) → (7) Security policy → (8) UTM inspection → (9) Egress NIC. Order matters for troubleshooting
questions.explanation: Knowing packet flow order is critical: routing determines egress interface (affects which policy matches). DNAT happens before policy check (so policy uses translated destination). UTM after policy allow. For site-to-site VPN: routing → policy → encrypt. Use 'diagnose debug flow' to trace packet.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Botnet C&C detection?
options: Identifies and blocks communication with known botnet command-and-control servers using FortiGuard IP reputation database — prevents infected hosts from receiving commands or exfiltrating data even without blocking the initial infection
questions.explanation: Botnet C&C: FortiGuard IP Reputation service maintains list of known bad IPs (C&C servers, spam sources, TOR exit nodes, etc.). Enable in security policy or IPS profile. Blocks outbound connections to known malicious IPs. Works at network layer — doesn't need SSL inspection.

questions.question: What is the difference between FortiGate explicit and transparent web proxy?
options: Explicit proxy: clients configure browser/device to use FortiGate as proxy (IP:port). Transparent proxy: FortiGate intercepts HTTP/HTTPS traffic without client configuration — clients unaware they're going through a proxy. Both allow user auth and URL inspection
questions.explanation: Explicit proxy: requires client configuration (PAC file, WPAD, or manual). Users must authenticate explicitly. Transparent: traffic intercepted by policy redirect — no client config needed, but harder to authenticate users. Transparent uses Web Cache Communication Protocol (WCCP) or policy-based redirect.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA)?
options: Identity-based access control that verifies user identity and device posture before granting per-application access — without network-level VPN. FortiGate acts as ZTNA access proxy: applications published privately, accessed via FortiClient with authentication
questions.explanation: ZTNA: replace VPN-based access. FortiClient registers to EMS (FortiClient EMS), device posture checked (OS version, AV status, compliance). User authenticated (LDAP/SAML). FortiGate access proxy provides per-app access tunnel. Never exposes network — only specific applications are accessible.

questions.question: What command diagnoses FortiGate session issues?
questions.explanation: 'diagnose sys session list': shows all active sessions with source/destination, interfaces, bytes, duration. 'diagnose sys session filter': filter sessions by IP, port, etc. 'diagnose sys session stat': session statistics (current, max). Key for troubleshooting connectivity: check if session exists and its NAT translation.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Security Fabric?
options: Fortinet's integrated security architecture connecting FortiGate, FortiSwitch, FortiAP, FortiClient, FortiAnalyzer, FortiSandbox — providing coordinated threat detection, automated response, and unified visibility across the network
questions.explanation: Security Fabric: FortiGate as root/downstream nodes. Devices join Fabric and share threat intelligence. Automated response: IOC detected on one device triggers block on all fabric devices. Fabric Connectors: integrate with cloud, SDN, ITSM. Fabric topology view in FortiGate GUI.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate policy route vs static route?
options: Static route: destination-based routing (forward traffic for subnet X via gateway Y). Policy route: source/application-based routing override — can match on source IP, incoming interface, destination IP, protocol/port and forward via a different gateway than static route dictates
questions.explanation: Policy routes checked BEFORE static routes. Match: source address, incoming interface, destination, protocol, port. Action: forward to gateway or change route. Use for: SD-WAN (deprecated in favor of SD-WAN rules), multi-WAN by traffic type, override routing decisions per application.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Geo-IP filtering?
options: Block or allow traffic by geographic location (country) of source/destination IP — uses FortiGuard geography IP database. Create geography-type address objects (select countries) and use in security policies. Useful for blocking known high-risk countries
questions.explanation: Geo-IP: FortiGuard database maps IP ranges to countries. Create geography address (e.g., Russia, China, North Korea). Use in policy source or destination. Common use: block inbound from non-operating-countries, block outbound to sanctioned regions. Also in VIP for restricting who can reach published servers.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's OSPF configuration and what interfaces need 'network' command?
options: OSPF neighbors form on interfaces included in 'network' statements. In FortiGate: define OSPF areas, add networks to areas. Interface must be in matching subnet for neighbor adjacency. Use 'get router info ospf neighbor' to verify adjacency formation
questions.explanation: FortiGate OSPF config: Network & Routing > OSPF. Add networks (subnets) to areas. Interfaces in matching subnets will participate. Verify: get router info ospf neighbor (adjacency), get router info ospf database (LSDB). 'diagnose ip router ospf all enable' for debug output.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's WAN optimization?
options: Reduces bandwidth consumption and improves performance for WAN-linked applications using: deduplication (removes repeated byte sequences), compression, web caching, protocol optimization (CIFS, FTP, HTTP, MAPI)
questions.explanation: WAN Opt: requires FortiGate on both ends (peer-to-peer). Byte caching: deduplication across connections. Web caching: store responses locally. Protocol optimization: CIFS/SMB optimization for file shares. Reduces effective bandwidth use by 40-90% for suitable traffic. Good for remote office over expensive WAN links.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's FortiOS diagnostic command for real-time packet capture?
options: diagnose sniffer packet INTERFACE FILTER COUNT VERBOSITY — captures packets on specific interface with BPF-style filter. Example: diagnose sniffer packet port1 'host 192.168.1.1' 4 0 (verbose=4 shows L2 headers, 0 = unlimited count)
questions.explanation: Packet sniffer: diagnose sniffer packet INTERFACE 'FILTER' VERBOSITY COUNT. INTERFACE: port1, any (all), internal. FILTER: BPF syntax (host X.X.X.X, port 80, tcp). VERBOSITY: 1 (basic), 4 (L2+L3+L4 headers), 6 (includes data). COUNT: 0=unlimited. Save to PCAP: add 'l' option and transfer.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's dynamic NAT (IP pool) overload mode?
options: PAT (Port Address Translation) — maps multiple internal IPs to one external IP using different source ports. Overload mode is the default: many internal devices share single external IP via port multiplexing. Used when ISP provides single public IP
questions.explanation: NAT modes: Overload (PAT/masquerade) — many-to-one with port allocation, default mode. One-to-One — map each internal IP to unique external IP. Fixed Port Range — assign port ranges per IP. No PAT — preserve source port. Overload most common for internet-facing with single IP.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's RADIUS authentication configuration?
options: RADIUS is not supported on FortiGate

Configure RADIUS server under User & Authentication > RADIUS Servers. Used for: admin authentication (System > Administrators), firewall user authentication (802.1X, VPN, policies). FortiGate sends Access-Request; RADIUS returns Access-Accept/Reject with optional attributes (group membership via VSA)
questions.explanation: FortiGate RADIUS: add server (IP, shared secret, authentication scheme). Use for: SSL-VPN user authentication, captive portal, 802.1X (FortiSwitch integration), admin authentication with 2FA (RSA SecurID via RADIUS). RADIUS VSA: return user group membership from RADIUS for policy matching.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's flow debug command sequence for troubleshooting?
options: Sequence: (1) diagnose debug reset, (2) diagnose debug flow filter addr X.X.X.X, (3) diagnose debug flow show function-name enable, (4) diagnose debug flow trace start 100, (5) diagnose debug enable — shows per-packet decision trace
questions.explanation: Flow debug shows exactly what FortiGate does with each packet: policy check result, NAT translation, route decision, security profile inspection. Essential troubleshooting tool. Always: reset first, set filter (specific IP prevents output flood), set trace count (100), enable, reproduce issue, disable when done.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's IPsec VPN Phase 1 and Phase 2?
options: Phase 1 (IKE): authenticates peers and establishes secure channel. Phase 2: negotiates encryption parameters for the actual data tunnel (IPsec SA). Phase 1 uses: pre-shared key or certificate, IKEv1 or IKEv2, encryption/auth algorithms, DH group. Phase 2: encryption for ESP/AH tunnel
questions.explanation: Phase 1 IKE: authentication + key exchange. Mode: Main or Aggressive (IKEv1), or IKEv2. Phase 2 IPsec: quick mode — negotiate ESP/AH parameters, create Security Associations (SAs). Lifetime: re-key before SA expires. Mismatch in any parameter → tunnel fails. Debug: diagnose vpn ike log filter name TUNNEL.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's URL category override and quota?
options: URL Override: allow specific URLs even when their category is blocked (exception list). URL Category Quota: limit time or data usage for specific categories per user per day (e.g., Social Media limited to 30 min/day). Both configured in Web Filter profiles
questions.explanation: Web filter overrides: URL exceptions bypass category blocks. FortiGuard category overrides: change rating for specific URL. Quotas: per-user daily limits (time or bandwidth) per category — requires user authentication for per-user tracking. Block page: customize with redirect URL or customized block message.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's FSSO (Fortinet Single Sign-On)?
options: Provides transparent user authentication by monitoring Windows AD logon events — the FSSO Collector Agent on Domain Controllers sends IP-to-username mappings to FortiGate in real-time. FortiGate maps IPs to users without requiring re-authentication
questions.explanation: FSSO modes: DC Agent mode (install agent on each DC, monitors Security event log), Polling mode (FortiGate polls DCs — less preferred), NTLM mode (browser auth). Collector Agent aggregates from multiple DCs. FortiGate gets IP-user mapping in <5 seconds of AD logon. Use in security policies as source 'user'.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Sandbox integration?
options: Submits suspicious files to FortiSandbox (on-premises or cloud) for dynamic analysis in an isolated environment — detects zero-day malware that signature-based AV misses. FortiSandbox executes the file and monitors behavior
questions.explanation: FortiSandbox integration: AV profile → enable FortiSandbox. Unknown files sent to sandbox for dynamic detonation (execute in VM, monitor: file system changes, network connections, registry modifications, process spawning). Verdict returned to FortiGate: allow or block. FortiCloud Sandbox: cloud-hosted alternative.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Source NAT and how is it configured in a policy?
options: In profile-based mode: enable NAT checkbox in security policy. In central NAT mode: create Central SNAT rule. IP Pool: define pool of external IPs. Overload mode (default PAT): uses firewall's egress interface IP if no pool defined. SNAT translates source IP for outbound connections
questions.explanation: SNAT options: Interface IP (use egress interface IP — dynamic, follows interface IP changes), IP Pool (specific pool of external IPs), Fixed Port (preserve source port — for some protocols). In policy: NAT checkbox + optional IP pool selection. Central NAT: separate SNAT table with explicit match criteria.

questions.question: What does 'diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic port1' show on FortiGate?
options: Physical NIC statistics: speed, duplex, MAC address, link status, receive/transmit packet counts, error counters, CRC errors — useful for diagnosing physical connectivity and NIC errors
questions.explanation: 'diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic INTERFACE': shows physical interface stats. Key fields: link up/down, speed/duplex negotiation, Rx/Tx packets, Rx/Tx bytes, errors (CRC, overruns, drops). CRC errors = cable/SFP issue. Speed mismatch = duplex mismatch. Compare with upstream switch port stats.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's local user versus remote user?
options: Local user: username/password stored directly on FortiGate. Remote user: authenticated against external server (LDAP/AD, RADIUS, TACACS+, SAML). Local users: for small deployments, VPN accounts. Remote users: enterprise scale, centralized management, password policy enforcement
questions.explanation: Local users: FortiGate stores credentials. Good for: small deployments, guest accounts, VPN. Remote users: FortiGate queries LDAP/RADIUS. Better for: enterprise scale, integration with corporate password policy. 2FA: can combine with local token or FortiToken. User groups from AD used in policies.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's DoS protection policy?
options: A separate policy type processed before security policies that protects against volumetric attacks: TCP/UDP/ICMP flood protection, port scan detection, source/destination threshold limits. Applied per interface to prevent resource exhaustion
questions.explanation: DoS policy: per interface, processed first (before routing/NAT/policy). Protections: TCP SYN flood (threshold + cookie challenge), UDP flood, ICMP flood, IP sweep, port scan. Stateless processing — doesn't require session table. Thresholds: trigger blocking at X packets/second. Different from security policy-based rate limiting.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate HA heartbeat and synchronization?
options: Dedicated connections between HA cluster members: heartbeat monitors peer health (heartbeat loss triggers failover), configuration sync (all config changes on primary replicate to secondary), session sync (active sessions replicated so failover is seamless)
questions.explanation: HA heartbeat: dedicated physical link(s) between units. Primary broadcasts heartbeat every 200ms. Secondary becomes primary if no heartbeat for dead-interval (default: 25 missed = 5 seconds). Sync: all configuration changes sync in ~1 second. Session sync: active TCP/UDP sessions replicated. Use dedicated cables for heartbeat (not shared with data traffic).

questions.question: What is FortiGate's web application firewall (WAF) capability?
options: Application layer (L7) protection for web servers: OWASP Top 10 detection, HTTP RFC compliance, signature-based attack detection (SQLi, XSS, CSRF, file inclusion), HTTP method restrictions, bot detection, brute-force protection for login pages
questions.explanation: WAF profile: enable in proxy inspection mode for inbound traffic to web servers. Signatures: SQLi, XSS, SSRF, command injection, path traversal. Constraints: max URL/header length, HTTP method allowlist. Known exploits: CVE signatures for web application vulnerabilities. Extended mode: custom signatures. Different from IPS (IPS is for all traffic, WAF is web-application specific).

questions.question: What is a FortiGate local CA and when is it used?
options: FortiGate can act as a Certificate Authority: generate root CA certificate, issue certificates for internal servers. Used for: SSL inspection (sign FortiGate's interception certificates), internal server certificates (no need for public CA), FortiGate admin certificate
questions.explanation: Local CA: System > Certificates > Create New > CA Certificate. Generate or import root CA. Use in SSL inspection profile (select as CA certificate). Issue server certificates for internal HTTPS servers. For SSL inspection, push root CA to client browsers via group policy for trust. Or import enterprise CA cert/key.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's FortiView and what does it show?
options: Real-time and historical traffic analytics dashboard: top sources, destinations, applications, users, threats, web categories, country-based traffic maps. Drill-down capability from summary to individual sessions. Data stored locally or in FortiAnalyzer
questions.explanation: FortiView: GUI dashboards under Dashboard > FortiView. Real-time (last 5 minutes with local log storage) or historical with FortiAnalyzer. Views: Traffic, Threats, Web, Applications, Users, Cloud, WiFi. Click any entry to drill down to sessions. Use for: capacity planning, security analysis, user activity monitoring.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate zone and when should you use it?
options: A logical grouping of interfaces — policies written to/from a zone apply to all interfaces in it. Simplifies policy management when multiple interfaces have the same security function (e.g., all internal LAN interfaces in one 'LAN' zone, all DMZ servers in 'DMZ' zone)
questions.explanation: Zones: simplify policy management. Instead of per-interface policies (5 LAN ports × 5 servers = 25 policies), use zones (1 LAN zone + 1 DMZ zone = 2 policies). Intra-zone: allow or deny traffic between interfaces in same zone. Common zones: LAN, WAN, DMZ, Guest, VoIP.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's 802.1X authentication for network access control?
options: Port-based network access control: clients authenticate before being allowed on the network. FortiGate can act as 802.1X authenticator for wired/wireless (with FortiSwitch/FortiAP). RADIUS server validates credentials and returns VLAN assignment for dynamic segmentation
questions.explanation: 802.1X with FortiGate/FortiSwitch: supplicant (device) → authenticator (switch/FortiGate) → RADIUS server. Authenticated: assigned to corporate VLAN. Failed: blocked or assigned guest VLAN. Dynamic VLAN assignment (RADIUS attribute 81). Machine authentication + user authentication for corporate devices + users.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Security Rating feature?
options: Automated assessment of FortiGate configuration against Fortinet security best practices — scores configuration on: device hardening, network visibility, breach detection, control posture. Shows actionable recommendations for improving security posture
questions.explanation: Security Rating: Dashboard > Security Rating. Checks: admin settings (MFA, password policy), logging, SSL inspection, firmware version, unused policies, weak cipher detection. Score 0-100 per category. Industry comparison. Remediation guidance per finding. Part of Fortinet Security Fabric visibility.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's VLAN configuration and what are the interface types?
options: VLAN interface: 802.1Q sub-interface tagged over physical interface. Software switch: bridge multiple physical ports (unmanaged switch behavior). Aggregate/LAG: bond multiple NICs for redundancy/throughput. Hard switch: hardware-offloaded switching on supported FortiGate models. VXLAN: Layer 2 over UDP tunnel
questions.explanation: Interface types: Physical (direct NIC), VLAN (sub-interface with 802.1Q tag), Software Switch (bridged ports), Hardware Switch (ASIC-accelerated bridge on supported models), Aggregate (LACP), Redundant (active/passive pair), WiFi (FortiAP SSID), VPN tunnel. Each can have its own IP, DHCP server, routing, and security policy.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate DHCP server and relay configuration?
options: FortiGate cannot be a DHCP server

FortiGate can run a DHCP server on any interface: define IP range, gateway, DNS servers, lease time. Can also act as DHCP relay (ip helper) — forward DHCP broadcasts to a centralized DHCP server on another network. FortiGate tracks IP-MAC mappings for asset identification
questions.explanation: DHCP server: per interface under Network > Interfaces > Edit > DHCP Server. Set range, exclusions, lease time, DNS, gateway, custom options. DHCP relay: System > Settings > DHCP relay — forward requests to server IP. Reserved DHCP: bind specific MAC to specific IP. FortiGate logs IP-to-MAC for policy use.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's NGFW application-based policy and how is it configured?
options: In NGFW mode: create a security policy using Application as the destination. Select specific apps (e.g., Facebook, YouTube) or application categories (Social Media, Video). No separate Application Control profile needed — app matching is in the policy itself. Requires proxy or flow inspection
Apps can only be blocked, not allowed
questions.explanation: NGFW policies: New Policy → Destination: select Application. FortiGate inspects traffic to identify application (first few packets), then applies policy. Multiple apps in one policy. Can combine with user authentication (User field in policy). NGFW mode is per-VDOM setting.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's connection to FortiAnalyzer?
options: FortiAnalyzer is a centralized log management and analytics platform — FortiGate sends all logs (traffic, security, system) to FortiAnalyzer via an encrypted connection. FortiAnalyzer provides: long-term log storage, compliance reports, cross-device correlation, FortiView with historical data
questions.explanation: FortiAnalyzer: log management + SIEM for Fortinet fabric. Configure on FortiGate: Log & Report > Log Settings > Remote Logging. Reliable syslog (TCP/514 or proprietary port 514/oftp). Reports: PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO compliance. Incident detection: correlate events across FortiGate, FortiMail, FortiWeb. Alternative: FortiCloud for cloud-based logging.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's two-factor authentication for admin access?
options: FortiGate supports: FortiToken (hardware or mobile TOTP app), email-based OTP, SMS OTP, and RADIUS-based 2FA. Configure per admin account: Require Two-Factor Authentication → assign FortiToken. Admin logs in with password + token code
questions.explanation: Admin 2FA: System > Administrators > Edit admin > Two-Factor Authentication. FortiToken Mobile: free app, TOTP. FortiToken hardware: physical OTP device. Email/SMS: less secure (send code to email/phone). RADIUS: delegate to RSA SecurID, Google Auth via RADIUS. FortiAuthenticator: scalable 2FA manager for large deployments.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's anti-spam filtering?
options: Inspects email traffic (SMTP, IMAP, POP3) for spam using: FortiGuard Anti-Spam service (IP reputation, DNS lookup), content analysis, DNSBL, heuristic scoring. Actions: tag subject, quarantine, block. Applies to both inbound and outbound email traffic
questions.explanation: FortiGate anti-spam profile: enable spam filtering on email protocols. Checks: FortiGuard spam definitions, URL/IP black lists, MIME type restrictions, keyword filtering. Best practice: FortiMail (dedicated email gateway) for enterprise email security. FortiGate anti-spam good for SMB deployments without dedicated email gateway.

questions.question: What is FortiGate explicit proxy ARP?
options: Proxy ARP: FortiGate responds to ARP requests for IP addresses that belong to downstream hosts — allows hosts in different subnets to communicate without a router hop visible. FortiGate answers ARP on behalf of hosts, then routes packets appropriately. Useful in specific single-subnet deployments
questions.explanation: Proxy ARP: enable on FortiGate interface. FortiGate replies to ARP requests for IPs it knows how to route. Common use: single /24 subnet split across FortiGate where hosts on different physical segments need to communicate. Also used in some HA configurations. Enable per-interface: config system interface → set proxy-arp enable.

questions.question: What are the FortiGate log types and where can logs be stored?
options: Log types: Traffic (firewall policy sessions), Event (system, admin actions, VPN, HA), Security (UTM events: AV, IPS, web filter, app control). Storage: Local disk (FortiGate flash), FortiAnalyzer (dedicated log server), FortiCloud (cloud-based), syslog server (any syslog receiver)
Logs can only be sent to syslog
questions.explanation: FortiGate logs: Traffic (forward/local/sniffer logs), Event (system events, VPN events, admin login, HA), Security (UTM: AV hits, IPS events, web filter blocks, app control). Destinations: local memory/disk (limited retention), FortiAnalyzer (primary for enterprise), FortiCloud (SaaS), CEF/syslog (SIEM integration).

questions.question: What is FortiGate's policy lookup diagnostic tool?
options: diagnose firewall iprope lookup SOURCE_IP DEST_IP PROTOCOL SRC_PORT DST_PORT INTERFACE — simulates policy match without generating real traffic. Shows which security policy would match and what action would be taken. Essential for validating policy configuration
questions.explanation: Policy lookup: diagnose firewall iprope lookup 192.168.1.100 8.8.8.8 6 1234 443 port1. Shows: matched policy ID, action, NAT translation. Use to verify policies before pushing changes. Also: GUI → Policy Lookup tool (Policy & Objects menu) for graphical interface version.

questions.question: What is FortiGate NP (Network Processor) and SP (Security Processor) hardware?
options: Hardware ASICs that offload specific processing from the main CPU: NP (Network Processor) — offloads firewall packet forwarding, IPsec encryption, NTurbo sessions. SP (Security Processor) — offloads SSL/TLS inspection, IPS/AV inspection. Dramatically increases throughput vs software processing
Same as ASIC in other vendors
questions.explanation: FortiGate ASICs: NP7/NP6 (network processor): offloads routing, NAT, basic firewall at line rate. CP9/CP8 (content processor / SP): offloads SSL, IPsec encryption. Different models have different ASIC configurations. Throughput specs: hardware-assisted >> software-only. Not all features benefit from offload (UTM inspection must go through CPU).

questions.question: What is FortiGate's session helper?
options: Application-level gateway (ALG) that handles protocols requiring dynamic port negotiation: FTP (creates helper for data connection), SIP (VoIP), TFTP, PPTP, H.323. Session helpers open pinholes in the firewall for secondary connections
questions.explanation: Session helpers: enable by default for common ALG protocols. FTP: PORT command tracking, opens data channel. SIP: SDP inspection, RTP/RTCP pinholes for voice. PPTP: GRE tracking for VPN. SIP helper critical for VoIP behind FortiGate NAT. Can conflict with SIP UTM profile — disable helper if using SIP profile.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's BGP configuration and route redistribution?
options: FortiGate supports BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) for dynamic routing: configure AS number, neighbors (iBGP/eBGP), route reflector capability. Redistribute: connected routes, static routes, OSPF routes into BGP. Use for: ISP peering, MPLS VPN PE routing, SD-WAN underlay routing
questions.explanation: BGP on FortiGate: config router bgp → set as (AS number), config neighbor (peer IP, remote-as). Redistribution: config redistribute connected/static. Route filtering: prefix-lists, route-maps. Use cases: dual ISP routing, MPLS cloud connectivity, SD-WAN spoke-to-hub routing (iBGP over IPsec). Verify: get router info bgp summary.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's FortiGate Cloud management?
options: SaaS-based cloud management platform for FortiGate devices — zero-touch provisioning, centralized configuration management, firmware updates, logging (FortiCloud Logging), and analytics without deploying on-premises FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer
questions.explanation: FortiGate Cloud: per-device or centralized management. Zero-touch deploy: pre-configure in cloud, ship FortiGate to remote site — device phones home and downloads config. Cloud logging: 7-30 day log retention (subscription). Alternative to FortiManager for smaller deployments. FortiCloud Sandbox integration available.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate password recovery procedure?
options: Boot FortiGate, interrupt boot with key press, select 'Restore Firmware' or maintenance boot. In maintenance mode: run 'execute factoryreset' or use special password recovery commands to reset admin password. Physical access required — cannot be done remotely
questions.explanation: Password recovery: requires physical or console access. Boot → interrupt with specific key (varies by model). Maintenance mode: reset admin password with 'execute password recovery' or similar. Some models: hold reset button for factory reset. Factory reset = all config lost. Always keep configuration backup.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's NTP configuration and why is it critical?
options: Accurate time is critical for: SSL certificate validation (expired cert blocking), log correlation with other systems, VPN IKE negotiation (skew > 5 minutes = tunnel failure), authentication token validation (TOTP codes expire). Config: System > Settings > NTP, or System > Settings → set timezone and NTP servers
questions.explanation: NTP config: System > Settings → enable NTP, add NTP server IP/FQDN. Verify: diagnose sys ntp status. Timezone: set correctly for local log timestamps. IKE/IPsec: peers must have time within ~5 minutes for IKEv1 (IKEv2 more tolerant). TOTP tokens: 30-second windows require accurate time. Use reliable internal NTP source or pool.ntp.org.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate captive portal?
options: Web-based authentication page presented to users before granting network access — intercepts HTTP/HTTPS and redirects to login page. Used for: guest network authentication, user identity tracking, acceptable use policy acknowledgment
questions.explanation: Captive portal: enable on interface (per VLAN/interface). Types: Authentication (user must log in with credentials), Disclaimer (acknowledge AUP). After auth: session bookmarked to user identity for policy and logging. Integration: local users, LDAP/RADIUS, social login (external). Guest management: create temporary accounts.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's deep packet inspection (DPI)?
options: Analyzes packet content (payload) beyond headers: identifies applications by content signatures regardless of port, detects malware in file transfers, inspects protocol compliance, extracts content for AV/IPS/DLP scanning. Requires more CPU than header inspection
questions.explanation: DPI: application layer inspection. Flow-based: stream inspection (faster). Proxy-based: full content buffering (more thorough). Both: identify applications by signature, not just port/protocol. Enable specific UTM profiles in security policy to activate DPI for AV, IPS, application control, web filter. SSL inspection enables DPI on encrypted traffic.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Inter-VDOM routing?
options: Inter-VDOM links connect two VDOMs within the same FortiGate — like virtual cables. Traffic between VDOMs goes through the virtual link and requires security policies on both VDOMs. Used to: route traffic between isolated VDOMs, apply different security policies per VDOM
questions.explanation: Inter-VDOM link: pair of virtual interfaces (one in each VDOM). Traffic between VDOMs: VDOM1-link1 → VDOM2-link2. Requires: static routes pointing to inter-VDOM link, security policy in both VDOMs allowing traffic. Common design: Root VDOM (internet), VDOM-A (tenant 1), VDOM-B (tenant 2) — inter-VDOM links for shared internet access.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's OSPF redistribution from connected routes?
options: Must explicitly configure: config router ospf → config redistribute connected → set status enable. Without this, directly connected routes on FortiGate interfaces are NOT advertised into OSPF (only OSPF-learned routes are). Also: redistribute static routes for static-to-dynamic injection
OSPF learns connected routes without config
questions.explanation: OSPF on FortiGate does NOT automatically redistribute connected routes. Must explicitly enable redistribution. Also configure network statements OR interface-based OSPF (passive interface for LAN segments to receive routes without forming neighbors). Common mistake: FortiGate connected routes missing from OSPF topology.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SSL certificate inspection for HTTPS?
options: Certificate Inspection: FortiGate reads the server certificate (SNI/CN) but does NOT decrypt content. Allows: URL category lookup by hostname, certificate validity checking, blocking expired/untrusted certs. Does NOT: allow AV, IPS, or DLP on HTTPS content. No CA certificate needed on clients
questions.explanation: SSL Certificate Inspection: SNI/subject extracted from TLS ClientHello and certificate. FortiGate can categorize URL and block bad certificates without decryption. Low performance impact, no client configuration. Full SSL inspection: decrypts content, high CPU, requires CA on clients. Balance: use certificate inspection for trusted sites, full for high-risk categories.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's conserve mode and when does it trigger?
options: FortiGate enters conserve mode when system memory drops below a critical threshold — starts dropping new sessions or blocking new connections to prevent system crash. Monitor with 'diagnose sys top' and 'get system performance status'. Triggered by: too many sessions, large UTM buffers, memory leaks
questions.explanation: Conserve mode: red alert for memory. Actions: (1) proxy-based inspection turned off (sessions bypass UTM), (2) new sessions blocked in extreme cases. Causes: too many concurrent sessions, large file scanning buffers, memory fragmentation. Resolution: tune session TTLs, reduce proxy buffer sizes, upgrade hardware, or add memory.

questions.question: What is FortiGate FortiLink and FortiSwitch integration?
options: A VPN between FortiGate and FortiSwitch

FortiLink is the management protocol allowing FortiGate to manage FortiSwitch as if it's an extension of the FortiGate — configure switch ports, VLANs, PoE, 802.1X from FortiGate GUI. FortiSwitch becomes part of Security Fabric. Managed via physical FortiLink port or VLAN over uplink
questions.explanation: FortiLink: discover and authorize FortiSwitch units. Manage from FortiGate: port assignment, VLANs, STP, LAG, PoE budgets, 802.1X policy, quarantine. Security posture: non-compliant devices quarantined via switch port VLAN change. FortiGate pushes security policy down to switch level. Zero-touch provisioning of new switches.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Application Control override?
options: Allows exceptions to application control policies — override a blocked application to allow it, or allow a category but block specific applications within it. Create overrides per user group or schedule (e.g., allow social media only after business hours)
questions.explanation: App Control overrides: in Application Control profile → Application Overrides. Select specific application → override action (allow, block, rate limit). Filter overrides: override entire category. Time-based: combine with security policy schedule. Per-group: different app control profiles for different user groups (IT vs. general staff).

questions.question: What is the FortiGate 'execute' command class used for?
options: Operational commands that perform actions: execute ping, execute traceroute, execute reboot, execute shutdown, execute backup config, execute restore config, execute factoryreset, execute ha failover, execute update-av (update AV database)
questions.explanation: FortiOS CLI structure: 'config' (configuration changes), 'get/show' (read configuration), 'diagnose' (diagnostics/debug), 'execute' (operational actions). Execute commands perform immediate actions: ping, traceroute, reboot, backup, restore, VPN operations (bring up/down), send test email/syslog, register with FortiGuard.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's VXLAN support?
options: VXLAN (Virtual eXtensible LAN): Layer 2 overlay over UDP/IP — FortiGate can terminate VXLAN tunnels to extend L2 segments across L3 networks. Used with: VMware NSX, overlay networks, multi-site L2 extension, connecting VMs across different physical networks
questions.explanation: FortiGate VXLAN: create VXLAN interfaces (VNI, VTEP IP). Traffic: encapsulate L2 frames in UDP/4789. Use cases: extend LAN across WAN without MPLS, connect to SDN overlays (VMware NSX-T), multi-tenant cloud environments. Combine with IPsec for encrypted VXLAN extension.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's ISDB (Internet Service Database)?
options: FortiGuard-maintained database of public internet services mapped to IP addresses and ports — allows policies based on named internet services (Microsoft 365, AWS, Salesforce, Google) instead of manually maintained IP lists. Auto-updated by FortiGuard
questions.explanation: ISDB: destination object type in security policies. Select 'Internet Service' as destination: choose Microsoft-Office365, Amazon-AWS, Google-GoogleBot, etc. FortiGuard maintains the IP/port mappings. Replaces manually maintained and outdated IP lists. Also used in SD-WAN rules for application-aware routing.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SIP profile and why disable the SIP session helper when using it?
options: SIP profile (in Application Control or UTM): deep SIP inspection for VoIP security (SIP authentication attacks, malformed SIP, SIP flooding). SIP session helper (ALG): handles NAT for SIP/RTP. If SIP profile is active WITH SIP helper, conflicts cause call failures — disable SIP helper when using SIP profile
questions.explanation: SIP conflict: session helper and SIP UTM profile both try to handle SIP NAT/inspection → duplicate processing causes one-way audio, call failures. Resolution: if using SIP UTM profile for inspection → disable SIP session helper (config system settings → set sip-helper disable). If no UTM inspection needed → keep SIP helper, disable SIP ALG in UTM.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's backup and restore procedure?
options: Backup: System > Dashboard > Status widget > System Information > Backup, or execute backup config {tftp/ftp/usb/management-station}. Backup includes: all policies, objects, settings, certificates, routing. Restore: same menu. Encrypted backup (with password) protects sensitive data like VPN keys
questions.explanation: FortiGate config backup: full config in .conf format (text). Options: unencrypted (readable text) or encrypted (binary with password). Include/exclude VPN secrets option. Best practice: encrypt backup files, store securely, backup before firmware upgrades. Restore: full restore replaces entire config. VDOM backup: backup individual VDOM configuration separately.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's FortiManager integration?
options: Centralized management platform for multiple FortiGate devices — single pane of glass for: policy management, firmware updates, configuration deployment, FortiGuard update management, revision history, change approval workflow, ADOM (administrative domain) separation
questions.explanation: FortiManager: manages 100s to 1000s of FortiGate devices. ADOMs: separate management domains per tenant/region. Policy packages: create once, deploy to multiple devices. Device groups: push updates to groups simultaneously. Revision history: rollback to previous configuration. Script management: automate CLI commands across devices.

questions.question: What are FortiGate NTP and DNS reliability considerations?
options: DNS: FortiGate uses DNS for FQDN objects (dynamic resolution), FortiGuard updates, and management hostname resolution. DNS failure: FQDN objects stop resolving → policy may fail open or closed. NTP: certificate validation, IPsec, TOTP all depend on accurate time. Use redundant NTP/DNS servers
DNS is only for web filtering
questions.explanation: DNS reliability: configure 2+ DNS servers (System > DNS). FQDN objects re-resolve periodically — if DNS down, FQDN object may resolve to stale IP. For FortiGuard connectivity: DNS must resolve update.fortiguard.net. NTP: configure 2+ NTP servers. Monitor both with SNMP/FortiMonitor. Single point of failure if only one DNS/NTP.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's layer 2 transparent mode deployment consideration?
options: In transparent mode: FortiGate forwards frames at L2 but still applies security policies. Considerations: (1) Only IP-based policies work (no user auth-based), (2) VLAN handling — can be VLAN-aware or forward all VLANs, (3) Must not break spanning tree, (4) Limited routing/NAT capabilities — no DHCP relay, no NAT
Transparent mode supports all UTM features equally
questions.explanation: Transparent mode limitations: no routing between interfaces, no NAT, limited DHCP functionality, MAC addresses passed through. Security: all UTM features work (AV, IPS, web filter). VLAN: forward specific VLANs or all with VLAN-aware mode. STP: FortiGate participates in STP to prevent loops. Best use: inserting security without IP changes.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's user quarantine feature?
options: Quarantines a device or user by: (1) blocking their traffic, (2) restricting to quarantine VLAN via FortiSwitch integration, (3) requiring re-authentication. Triggered manually or automatically (by IPS detecting high-severity threat, FortiClient posture non-compliance, or FortiAnalyzer IOC detection)
questions.explanation: Quarantine: automatic when threat level exceeds threshold (IPS sensor → quarantine attacker). Manual: User > Monitor > Quarantine. Integration: FortiSwitch changes port VLAN to quarantine VLAN. FortiClient EMS: quarantine non-compliant devices. Release quarantine: manually or after timeout. Quarantine log shows reason.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's cloud application visibility with FortiSASE?
options: FortiSASE extends FortiGate's security model to cloud-delivered SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) — provides Secure Internet Access (SIA) with FortiGate capabilities in the cloud for remote users without full VPN, using nearest FortiSASE PoP
questions.explanation: FortiSASE: cloud-delivered security service based on FortiOS. Components: SIA (direct internet access through PoP), SD-WAN (FortiSASE as hub), zero-trust network access. FortiClient connects users to nearest FortiSASE PoP for consistent policy enforcement regardless of location. Managed from FortiManager or FortiSASE portal.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's protocol recognition in Application Control?
options: App Control identifies thousands of applications by behavioral/signature patterns regardless of port — P2P, social media, VoIP, gaming, cloud storage. Even if an application uses port 443, FortiGate identifies it as the specific app (Facebook, Netflix, Dropbox). Requires at least first few packets of session
questions.explanation: Deep application inspection: some apps identifiable in first packet (TLS ClientHello SNI), others require more packets or SSL inspection (for HTTPS apps). Application Control database: 3000+ applications. Custom signatures: define your own app signatures. Confidence score: some apps identified with uncertainty — configurable threshold.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's policy consolidation best practice?
options: Use specific, least-privilege policies but consolidate where security requirements are same. Consolidation reduces: policy lookup time, admin overhead. Avoid: any/any deny at top, overlapping policies creating confusion. Use address groups and service groups to merge similar policies. Regular review: remove unused policies
questions.explanation: Policy best practices: (1) Specific on top, general below (first-match applies). (2) Most-used policies near top (performance). (3) Use groups (address, service, user) to minimize policy count. (4) Implicit deny at bottom (no explicit deny needed). (5) Disable unused policies instead of deleting (audit trail). (6) Use policy comments for documentation.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SNMP monitoring configuration?
options: Configure SNMP community or SNMP v3 user under System > SNMP. Enable per management interface. FortiGate MIB: provides all system metrics (CPU, memory, sessions, interface stats, VPN status). Traps: send alerts for HA events, interface up/down, CPU/memory thresholds, VPN tunnel events
questions.explanation: SNMP on FortiGate: System > SNMP. v1/v2c: community strings (read-only or read-write). v3: username, auth (MD5/SHA) + privacy (DES/AES). Enable on specific management interfaces. Traps: configure trap server IP + port. MIB download: available from Fortinet support portal. Poll: interface traffic, CPU, session count, VPN status.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's routing monitor command?
options: get router info routing-table all / get router info routing-table details PREFIX — shows FIB (Forwarding Information Base). 'diagnose ip route list' shows kernel routing table. 'get router info ospf neighbor' for OSPF status. 'get router info bgp summary' for BGP
questions.explanation: Routing diagnostics: 'get router info routing-table all' (RIB — routing table). 'diagnose ip route list' (kernel FIB — what's actually used for forwarding). Prefix: 'get router info routing-table details 192.168.1.0/24'. Protocol-specific: ospf, bgp, rip commands under 'get router info'. Policy routes: 'diagnose ip policy list'.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's security profile group?
options: Bundle multiple UTM security profiles (AV, Web Filter, IPS, App Control, DNS Filter, SSL Inspection) into a named group — apply the group to security policies instead of attaching profiles individually. Simplifies policy management and ensures consistent profile combinations across policies
questions.explanation: Profile groups: Security Profiles > Profile Groups > New. Combine: AV profile + Web Filter profile + IPS sensor + App Control profile. Apply to policy once. Change the group → all policies using that group updated. Great for: standardized security levels (Basic, Standard, High) applied to different policy classes.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) use case?
options: Sub-second failure detection for routing protocol adjacencies — BFD runs independently between neighbors and signals routing protocol (OSPF/BGP) to withdraw routes immediately when link fails rather than waiting for routing protocol dead timer (could be 40+ seconds for OSPF)
questions.explanation: BFD: lightweight hello protocol, 300ms default. OSPF dead timer default: 40 seconds. BGP hold timer: 90 seconds. With BFD: detect failure in 3 × 300ms = 900ms. Enable: config router bfd → config neighbor. Associate with OSPF/BGP: set bfd enable under router protocol config. Use for: mission-critical routing where fast convergence required.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's inline sandbox (FortiSandbox inline) mode?
options: FortiSandbox inline mode: files are HELD (blocked) until sandbox analysis completes rather than allow-and-analyze. Prevents zero-day files from reaching users even on first encounter. Trade-off: latency for file downloads. Alternative: block-override (download allowed with warning, sandboxing in background)
questions.explanation: Sandbox modes: (1) Standard: send file, allow immediately, block if verdict = malware (only blocks on second encounter). (2) Inline hold: send file, block download until verdict (effective but adds latency). (3) File filter: block file types before sandbox (pre-filter). Inline hold recommended for high-security deployments despite latency impact.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's certificate-based admin authentication?
options: Instead of (or in addition to) password, admins authenticate with a client PKI certificate — certificate identifies admin, may be combined with 2FA. Configure: System > Administrators > Edit > PKI. Certificate presented during HTTPS session. Mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication for zero-trust admin access
questions.explanation: PKI admin auth: select PKI as authentication type for admin account. CA certificate: import CA that issued admin certificates. Admin presents certificate during browser login (prompted). No password or in addition to password. CA-signed certificates: more secure than passwords (can't be guessed). Requires clients to have cert installed.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's session acceleration and NP offload?
options: Network Processor (NP) offload: after first few packets establish session and policy match, subsequent packets bypass the main CPU and are processed entirely in NP hardware at line rate. Requires: offload-compatible interface (NP-connected), allow in config, feature must not require CPU processing (no UTM)
questions.explanation: NP offload (fastpath): after session established and first packets processed, NP handles forwarding for remaining packets of same session. Traffic NOT offloaded: sessions with UTM inspection (AV, IPS), SSL inspection (proxy-based), software switch. Offload check: diagnose sys session list → look for 'offload' flag. Massively increases throughput for bulk traffic.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate RADIUS dynamic VLAN assignment?
options: RADIUS server returns Tunnel-Type=VLAN (13), Tunnel-Medium-Type=802 (6), Tunnel-Private-Group-ID=VLAN_ID attributes in Access-Accept — FortiGate (or FortiSwitch in 802.1X) assigns user's port to specified VLAN dynamically. Enables per-user dynamic network segmentation without manual config
questions.explanation: Dynamic VLAN: 802.1X auth → RADIUS returns VLAN attributes → FortiSwitch moves port to user's VLAN. RADIUS VSA (Fortinet-Group-Name) returns user group for FortiGate policy matching. Combine: VLAN assignment (where user lands) + user group (what they can access). Use for: BYOD (guest VLAN), contractors (restricted VLAN), employees (corporate VLAN).

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SD-WAN quality monitoring?
options: Continuous measurement of WAN link quality metrics: latency (RTT), jitter (variance), and packet loss per link. Performance SLA: define probes (HTTP, DNS, ping to target server), set thresholds. SD-WAN rules route applications to links meeting SLA. Alert: notify when link degrades
questions.explanation: SD-WAN Performance SLA: configure probe target (8.8.8.8, specific server), probe interval, threshold (latency < 50ms, jitter < 10ms, packet loss < 1%). Link health status updated continuously. SD-WAN rules: if primary link exceeds SLA thresholds, failover to secondary link automatically. Historical graphs: track link quality over time.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's IPS engine rate limiting and threshold tuning?
options: IPS thresholds prevent false positives: rate-based signatures trigger when packet rate exceeds threshold (e.g., detect port scan only if >X ports scanned/second). Tuning: increase threshold to reduce false positives, decrease to increase sensitivity. Add exceptions for known-good traffic patterns
questions.explanation: IPS tuning: (1) Disable specific signatures causing FPs. (2) Add filter-based exceptions (source IP, destination IP). (3) Rate-based signatures: adjust threshold. (4) Custom signature: create precise detection rules. (5) IPS sensor: multiple sensors with different profiles for different network segments. Monitor IPS events in FortiView Security > IPS.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SAML integration for admin SSO?
options: FortiGate can act as SAML Service Provider — admin logs into corporate IdP (Okta, Azure AD, ADFS), FortiGate validates SAML assertion for admin access. No need for separate FortiGate password — SSO with corporate credentials, inherits MFA from IdP. Configure: System > Admin SSO > SAML
questions.explanation: SAML SP for admin: create admin account with matching username, set authentication to SAML. Admin accesses FortiGate login → redirected to IdP. After SSO, redirected back with assertion. Admin profile mapped from SAML attribute (group claim). Benefits: centralized auth, IdP MFA inherited, no FortiGate-specific passwords to manage.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's explicit proxy vs transparent proxy best use cases?
options: Explicit proxy: better user authentication (users know they're going through proxy, authenticate explicitly), pac file distribution for granular control, works well for managed devices. Transparent: better for BYOD or unmanaged devices that won't have proxy settings, no user config required — use with FSSO for auth
questions.explanation: Choose based on device management: Managed corporate devices → explicit proxy (push PAC file via GPO, user auth works). Unmanaged/BYOD/IoT → transparent (no device config). Transparent with FSSO: get user identity without captive portal. Some protocols don't work through explicit proxy (non-HTTP) — those bypass and go through regular firewall policy.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's GTP (GPRS Tunneling Protocol) inspection?
options: Carrier-grade inspection for mobile core networks — FortiGate can inspect and filter GTP traffic between GPRS support nodes (GGSN/SGW/PGW). Validates: GTP header fields, IMSI/MSISDN filtering, GTP-C flooding protection, tunnel ID spoofing prevention. Required for telecom/carrier FortiGate deployments
questions.explanation: GTP inspection: FortiGate carrier features for mobile operators. GTP-C (control) and GTP-U (user data) inspection. Protect against: GTP flooding (DDoS on mobile core), IMSI spoofing, invalid message types, tunnel hijacking. Requires carrier-grade FortiGate models. Not relevant for enterprise deployments.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's config revision and change management?
options: FortiGate maintains a local revision history of configuration changes — view at System > Config > Revisions. Compare revisions (diff). Restore to previous revision. Each revision shows: timestamp, admin who made change, number of changes. Best practice: take named backup before major changes
questions.explanation: Config revisions: System > Configuration > Revisions. Automatic: every config change creates revision. Manual: add description to important revisions. Compare: diff view shows exactly what changed between revisions. Restore: roll back to specific revision. Limit: finite number stored (older pruned). FortiManager: central revision management across all devices.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's security connector for AWS/Azure/GCP?
options: Cloud-native connectors that dynamically update address objects based on cloud infrastructure tags/labels — automatically include/exclude cloud VMs from security policies based on their cloud metadata (instance ID, tags, VPC). No manual IP updates needed when cloud resources scale
questions.explanation: Fabric Connectors: AWS (EC2 tags, Security Groups, VPC), Azure (resource groups, tags, subscriptions), GCP (labels, projects). Dynamic address objects sync with cloud API. When new EC2 with tag 'Role=WebServer' launches → automatically added to 'AWS-WebServers' address object. Policies update in real-time without admin intervention.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's ECMP (Equal-Cost Multi-Path) routing?
options: Routes traffic across multiple equal-cost paths to same destination — load balancing across multiple WAN links or equal-cost paths. Methods: source IP hash, session round-robin, spillover (primary until full, then overflow). Configured in static routes with same metric on multiple gateways
questions.explanation: ECMP: add multiple static routes with same destination and equal distance/metric but different gateways. Load balance methods (config router setting): source-ip-based (same source always goes same path — good for NAT), round-robin (session-based), weighted (different traffic ratios per link), spillover (bandwidth-based overflow). Different from SD-WAN (SD-WAN has more intelligence).

questions.question: What is FortiGate's interface-based routing vs policy-based routing priority?
options: Policy routes are checked FIRST before interface/static routing table — policy route match overrides static/dynamic routing. If no policy route matches, falls back to routing table. Policy routes checked top-to-bottom (like security policies). Use carefully: unintended policy routes can override expected routing behavior
questions.explanation: Processing order: Policy Routes → Routing Table (static, dynamic, connected). Policy route match overrides everything. Add policy routes only for specific overrides. Common mistake: too-broad policy route redirecting unexpected traffic. Debug: diagnose ip policy list shows policy routes, diagnose ip route list shows kernel FIB after policy route application.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's web filter safe search enforcement?
options: Forces safe search settings on major search engines (Google, Bing, YouTube) by injecting safe search parameters into HTTP requests — even if user doesn't use safe search mode, FortiGate overrides it. Part of Web Filter profile. Useful for schools, family filtering
questions.explanation: Safe search: Web Filter profile → Content Filter → Safe Search. FortiGate rewrites search queries to include safe search parameters. Google: appends safe=strict. YouTube: restricted mode via HTTPS header or DNS-based enforcement. Requires proxy inspection (or DNS filtering for DNS-based method). Also: Google Apps restrictions (restrict to specific org domain).

questions.question: What is FortiGate's FortiToken Two-Factor Authentication workflow?
options: User enters username + password → FortiGate prompts for token code → user checks FortiToken Mobile app (or hardware token) → enters 6-digit TOTP code → FortiGate validates against token seed → access granted. Token changes every 30 seconds
Token is sent via email only
questions.explanation: FortiToken workflow: TOTP (Time-based OTP). Seed shared between FortiToken app and FortiGate during provisioning. Each 30-second window generates same 6-digit code. FortiGate validates: HMAC-SHA1(seed + time). Clock sync critical (±1 window tolerance). Activation: email QR code to user. FortiToken Mobile: iOS/Android app. Hardware token: USB/LCD device.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's IPsec remote access VPN with FortiClient?
options: IPsec remote access: FortiClient IKE/IPsec implementation. IKEv2 + EAP (username/password) or certificate auth. Split tunneling: route specific subnets through VPN. FortiClient EMS manages VPN profiles centrally. Advantages: better performance than SSL-VPN for bulk transfer, native OS integration on Windows/macOS
questions.explanation: FortiClient IPsec: IKEv2 recommended (faster re-key, more robust than IKEv1). EAP-MSCHAPv2 for username/password. Certificate auth for stronger security. FortiClient EMS: pre-configure VPN settings for users, enforce compliance before VPN allow. Split tunneling: corporate traffic through VPN, internet direct. Always-on VPN option for corporate devices.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's LLDP (Link Layer Discovery Protocol) support?
options: IEEE 802.1AB protocol: FortiGate transmits/receives LLDP frames to discover directly connected neighbors and advertise capabilities. Uses: network documentation, detect unexpected devices, verify topology. LLDP-MED: extended for IP phones — advertise VLAN assignment to VoIP devices
questions.explanation: LLDP on FortiGate: enabled per interface. View neighbors: diagnose netlink lldp neighbor. Information: device ID, capabilities, management IP, VLANs, port description. LLDP-MED: send voice VLAN ID to IP phones automatically. FortiGate advertises itself as: FortiGate device, firmware version, capability flags. CDP (Cisco Discovery Protocol) also supported on FortiGate.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's management access control best practice?
options: Restrict management access: (1) Enable only HTTPS (not HTTP) for GUI, (2) Restrict source IPs allowed to management (trusted hosts per admin account), (3) Disable PING on WAN-facing interfaces, (4) Enable Lockout for failed logins, (5) Use strong passwords + 2FA, (6) Dedicated management interface/VLAN
questions.explanation: Hardening: Admin trusted hosts (IPv4/IPv6 source IPs allowed per admin), disable HTTP (only HTTPS), disable SSH from untrusted networks, admin timeout (auto-logout), failed login lockout, disable SNMP on WAN, disable ping on WAN, dedicated management interface. Security Rating feature identifies misconfigurations automatically.

questions.question: What is the difference between FortiGate policy deny and policy implicit deny?
options: Explicit deny: creates a log entry when matched — useful for auditing blocked traffic. Implicit deny: the built-in default rule at the bottom (all traffic not matched by any policy is denied without logging). Adding explicit deny rules at bottom allows logging of blocked traffic for security monitoring
questions.explanation: FortiGate implicit deny: traffic not matching any policy is silently dropped (no log by default). Explicit deny policy: add at bottom with logging enabled → all denied traffic logged. Use for: compliance (must log all denied traffic), troubleshooting (see what's being blocked), SIEM visibility. Enable: create policy with action=deny + log enabled.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's session table maximum and impact when full?
options: Each FortiGate model has a maximum concurrent session limit (e.g., 50K for entry-level, 10M+ for high-end). When table is full: new sessions dropped (TCP: RST sent, UDP: silently dropped). Monitor: get system performance status → session usage %. Tune: reduce session TTL for UDP/ICMP, implement DoS protection
questions.explanation: Session table capacity: model-dependent. Monitor: 'get system performance status'. Session limits: UDP (5 sec default), ICMP (5 sec), TCP half-open (30 sec), TCP established (3600 sec). Tune TTLs: config system session-ttl for UDP/ICMP. DoS policies: rate limit per IP to prevent single source exhausting table. Conserve mode: automatic protection when memory low.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SD-WAN tie-breaking when multiple rules match?
options: SD-WAN rules: first matching rule applies (top-to-bottom, similar to security policies). Multiple rules with same match criteria: most specific wins. SD-WAN interfaces within a rule: LOWEST cost/latency member selected based on load balance algorithm (volume, sessions, spillover, measured SLA). Default: all traffic via lowest cost member
questions.explanation: SD-WAN rule order matters: most specific at top (specific application + specific source), least specific at bottom (catch-all). Within a rule, member selection: configured load balance method. Best Member: selected based on SLA criteria. Preferred members list in rule: ordered preference list with fallback.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's MAC-based VLAN assignment?
options: Assign VLAN based on source MAC address — devices with specific MACs automatically placed in designated VLAN. Useful for: devices that can't do 802.1X (printers, IP phones), pre-staged device placement. Configure on FortiGate/FortiSwitch interface MAC table or in RADIUS with MAC-auth bypass
questions.explanation: MAC-auth bypass (MAB): fallback when device fails 802.1X. RADIUS authenticates device by MAC address (format: 00-11-22-33-44-55 or similar). Returns VLAN assignment for that MAC. Use: printers, cameras, IoT — not 802.1X capable. Security: MAC can be spoofed — less secure than 802.1X. OK for low-security devices in isolated VLAN.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's graceful failover in HA?
options: When HA failover occurs: TCP sessions (with session sync enabled) are maintained on the new primary — existing connections continue without interruption. Unsynchronized sessions (UDP, ICMP, or sessions after last sync) are dropped and must be re-established by applications
questions.explanation: HA session sync: TCP sessions replicated every 50ms (configurable). On failover: <200ms for simple failover. Synced sessions continue. Unsynced (new since last sync, or UDP/ICMP without state sync) dropped → application retries. VPN sessions: IPsec SAs replicated. SSL-VPN: may need to reconnect. Session sync requires dedicated sync interface on some models.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's diagnose sys top command?
options: Shows real-time process CPU and memory usage — displays top processes consuming resources. Use to identify: high CPU processes (IPS daemon, proxy daemon, etc.), memory consumers. Press 'q' to quit. Shows: PID, process name, CPU%, MEM%, status
questions.explanation: 'diagnose sys top': Linux-like top for FortiOS. Key processes: proxyd (proxy inspection), ipsengine (IPS), sslvpn, pyfcgid (Python services), dnsproxy. High CPU on proxyd: too many proxy sessions or large files. IPS engine high: DPI processing. Use with 'get system performance status' for system-wide view. 'diagnose sys process pstack PID' for stack trace.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's WAN link load balancing strategies?
options: SD-WAN load balancing methods: (1) Volume: balance by bandwidth used. (2) Sessions: balance by session count. (3) Spillover: use primary until bandwidth threshold, overflow to secondary. (4) Source-IP: consistent path per source IP. (5) Measured SLA: route to lowest latency/loss member meeting SLA criteria
Only one WAN interface per FortiGate
