questions.explanation: SD-WAN algorithms in rule: volume (equal bandwidth distribution), sessions (equal session count), spillover (primary full → use secondary), source-ip-hash (same source → same link, good for NAT). Best member: SLA-based. Combine: spillover for bulk + SLA-based for voice/video. Weighted: percentage-based split (70%/30%).

questions.question: What is FortiGate's application rate limiting (bandwidth policy)?
options: Apply bandwidth limits per application or application category using traffic shaping: (1) Guaranteed bandwidth (reserved), (2) Maximum bandwidth (ceiling), (3) Priority (for queuing). Apply to specific applications in security policy or Application Control profile. Rate limit: 'streaming video limited to 5Mbps total'
questions.explanation: Traffic shaping with App Control: create traffic shaper (shared for total category, per-IP for individual limit). Apply in security policy → Traffic Shaping tab. Example: YouTube category → max 5Mbps shared across all users. VoIP → guaranteed 1Mbps + priority 1. Prevents any single application from consuming all bandwidth.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's IPv6 support?
options: Full IPv6 support: IPv6 addresses on interfaces, IPv6 security policies, IPv6 routing (static, OSPFv3, BGP, RIPng), IPv6 NAT (NPTv6, NAT64), dual-stack operation (IPv4+IPv6 simultaneously), IPv6 VPN. Security profiles work on IPv6 traffic. FortiGuard updates include IPv6 threat intelligence
questions.explanation: IPv6 config: interface → IPv6 tab → assign IPv6 address. Policies: source/destination supports IPv6 objects. Routing: configure separately from IPv4. NAT64: translate between IPv6 clients and IPv4 servers. NAT46: IPv4 clients to IPv6 servers. Dual stack: run both protocols simultaneously. DHCPv6 server: supported on interfaces. RA (Router Advertisement) configuration.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate FGCP (FortiGate Cluster Protocol) election process?
options: HA election: device with HIGHEST priority becomes primary (default priority = 128, range 0-255). Tie: highest serial number wins. Override: enable 'override' to maintain primary role after recovery (without override: recovered device rejoins as secondary even if higher priority). Election uses heartbeat interface
questions.explanation: FGCP election: (1) Compare HA priority — higher number = primary. (2) If equal priority: compare uptime. (3) If equal uptime: compare serial number (higher = primary). Override mode: with override enabled, a unit with higher priority that recovers will preempt current primary (planned failback). Without override: stability preferred (no preemption).

questions.question: What is the purpose of Fortinet's Security Fabric?
options: An integrated cybersecurity architecture connecting all Fortinet products to share threat intelligence, coordinate policies, and provide unified visibility across the entire network
questions.explanation: Security Fabric: FortiGate as the core, connected to FortiAnalyzer, FortiManager, FortiClient, FortiAP, FortiSwitch, and other Fortinet products. Shares IoC data, enables single-pane management, automated threat response across all connected devices.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Intrusion Prevention System (IPS)?
options: Inspects network traffic for known exploit signatures and anomalous behavior, blocking attacks in real-time — uses signature-based detection plus protocol anomaly detection. Applied in firewall policies as a security profile
questions.explanation: FortiGate IPS: inline inspection on all sessions. Signature database updated via FortiGuard. IPS profiles: default, protect_client, protect_server. Enable in firewall policy. Performance impact: varies by throughput — use NP/CP ASICs for hardware acceleration.

questions.question: What is the difference between FortiGate flow-based and proxy-based inspection?
options: Flow-based: inspects packets as they flow through without buffering — faster, less CPU, but less thorough. Proxy-based: buffers the full content before inspection — slower, more thorough, enables full content inspection (AV, DLP, SSL deep inspection)
questions.explanation: Flow-based: first-packet inspection, no buffering, good for throughput-sensitive environments. Proxy-based: full content buffering, better detection rates (especially for AV), required for some features (WAF, email inspection). Configured per security profile and VDOM inspection mode.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate VDOM (Virtual Domain)?
options: A logical partition of a FortiGate device that operates as an independent firewall with its own interfaces, routing table, policies, and administration — enables multi-tenancy on a single physical appliance
questions.explanation: VDOMs: split one FortiGate into multiple independent firewalls. Root VDOM: default, handles management. Traffic VDOM: separate security domain. Inter-VDOM links: virtual interfaces connecting VDOMs. Each VDOM has own interfaces, routes, policies, administrator accounts.

questions.question: What is FortiGate SSL VPN and how does it differ from IPsec VPN?
options: SSL VPN: clientless (web portal) or FortiClient-based, uses TCP 443 (HTTPS), traverses firewalls/NAT easily, per-application access. IPsec VPN: site-to-site or client-to-site, UDP 500/4500, better for high-throughput, standard-based for interoperability
SSL VPN doesn't require a client
questions.explanation: SSL VPN modes: Web mode (browser only, clientless), Tunnel mode (FortiClient, full network access). IPsec: standard protocol, hardware-accelerated by NP ASICs, better for permanent site-to-site tunnels. SSL VPN: better for remote access users behind NAT/firewalls.

questions.question: What is FortiGuard and what services does it provide?
options: Fortinet's cloud-based threat intelligence and security subscription service providing: IPS signatures, antivirus, web filtering categories, anti-spam, application control signatures, IP reputation, and botnet C&C updates to FortiGate
questions.explanation: FortiGuard services: updated hourly/daily. IPS: vulnerability signatures. AV: malware signatures. Web Filter: URL categorization (75+ categories). App Control: application signatures. Anti-Spam: email spam detection. IP Reputation: known malicious IPs. DNS Filter: malicious domain blocking.

questions.question: How does FortiGate application control work?
options: Identifies applications regardless of port using deep packet inspection and behavioral signatures — can allow/block/monitor specific apps (Facebook, BitTorrent, Zoom) even when they use non-standard ports or encryption
questions.explanation: App control signatures from FortiGuard identify thousands of applications. Works at L7. Can: allow, block, monitor, shape (QoS). Applied in firewall policies as Application Control profile. Deep SSL inspection required to identify encrypted apps. Can override web filter for specific apps.

questions.question: What is FortiGate web filtering?
options: Inspects HTTP/HTTPS URLs and categorizes them against FortiGuard Web Filter database — allows administrators to block/allow entire categories (gambling, social media, malware) or specific URLs. SafeSearch enforcement, YouTube restriction also available
questions.explanation: Web filter: profile applied in firewall policy. Modes: FortiGuard categories (cloud lookup), local categories, regex/URL lists. FortiGuard: 75+ categories, real-time updates. Override: temporary category change by authenticated user. SSL deep inspection required for HTTPS filtering.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate firewall policy and what are the required matching criteria?
options: Must specify: Source Interface, Destination Interface, Source Address, Destination Address, Schedule, Service (port/protocol), Action (ACCEPT/DENY/IPSEC). Without all fields, policy won't match. Evaluated top-down, first match wins
questions.explanation: Policy matching order: incoming interface → source address → outgoing interface → destination address → service → schedule → user/group. First matching policy action applied. Implicit deny at bottom (all traffic not matching any policy is dropped). Policy ID order matters.

questions.question: What is FortiGate NAT and what types are available?
options: Source NAT (SNAT): translates internal source IP to external IP for outbound traffic. Destination NAT (DNAT/VIP): translates external destination IP to internal server IP for inbound traffic. Policy NAT vs Central SNAT table
NAT is not available on FortiGate
questions.explanation: SNAT: enable NAT in outbound policy (use outgoing interface IP or IP pool). DNAT: create Virtual IP (VIP) — maps external IP:port to internal server IP:port. Central SNAT: alternative to per-policy NAT, centralized table. NAT46/NAT64 for IPv4-IPv6 translation.

questions.question: What is FortiGate high availability (HA) and what modes are available?
options: Active-Passive (A-P): primary handles traffic, secondary standby — failover on primary failure, minimal performance overhead. Active-Active (A-A): both devices process traffic via load balancing — better throughput, more complex. HA uses heartbeat link for synchronization
questions.explanation: HA cluster: heartbeat interfaces (dedicated physical interfaces). Session synchronization (configurable). Config sync automatic. HA priority: higher priority = primary. Preempt mode: primary recovers and takes back role. A-A: FortiGate uses SPU to distribute sessions.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Security Profiles and how are they applied?
options: Modular inspection features (AV, IPS, Web Filter, App Control, Email Filter, DLP, SSL Inspection) configured as named profiles and attached to firewall policies — only applied to traffic matching the policy
questions.explanation: Security profiles: created independently, attached to policies. Traffic matches policy → security profiles inspect the session. Profiles: Antivirus, IPS, Web Filter, Application Control, Email Filter, DLP, File Filter, SSL/SSH Inspection. Profile mode determines depth of inspection.

questions.question: How does FortiGate SSL deep inspection work?
options: FortiGate acts as a man-in-the-middle: decrypts SSL/TLS traffic, inspects content, re-encrypts with its own certificate — requires trusting the FortiGate CA certificate on client devices. Enables AV, IPS, Web Filter on HTTPS traffic
questions.explanation: SSL deep inspection: FortiGate presents its own signed cert to client (impersonating the server). Must push FortiGate's CA cert to all clients (GPO, MDM). Certificate inspection (no decryption): checks cert validity only — lighter, misses content threats. Full SSL inspection: decrypts and inspects everything.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's antivirus scanning and what protocols does it cover?
options: Inspects files in HTTP, HTTPS (with SSL inspection), FTP, SMTP, IMAP, POP3, CIFS/SMB, MAPI — uses FortiGuard signatures plus heuristic and AI-based detection. Quarantine infected files option available
questions.explanation: FortiGate AV: scan all major protocols. Modes: flow-based (fast, pattern matching on stream) and proxy-based (buffer full file, better detection). FortiGuard: cloud lookup for unknown files (sandbox option). Large file threshold: skip scanning files over size limit to prevent performance impact.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate Virtual IP (VIP) and how is it used?
options: A NAT mapping that translates an external public IP (or IP:port) to an internal server IP:port — used to publish internal servers to the internet. Traffic arrives at external IP, FortiGate NATs to internal server. Must create firewall policy using VIP as destination
questions.explanation: VIP types: Static NAT (1:1 IP mapping), Port Forwarding (external IP:port → internal IP:port), Load Balance (one VIP → multiple servers). Create VIP object → use as destination in inbound firewall policy. Source IP in policy is external clients; destination is the VIP object.

questions.question: What is FortiGate traffic shaping (QoS)?
options: Controls bandwidth allocation for different traffic types — per-policy traffic shaping sets guaranteed/maximum bandwidth and priority. Traffic shapers define bandwidth limits. Shapes outbound traffic; cannot shape inbound (use ingress policing)
questions.explanation: Traffic shapers: shared (total bandwidth across all policies using it) or per-IP (bandwidth per source IP). Apply in firewall policy: guaranteed bandwidth, max bandwidth, priority (high/medium/low). DSCP marking available. Use for: prioritizing VoIP, limiting video streaming, ensuring business app bandwidth.

questions.question: What is FortiGate OSPF configuration?
options: FortiGate supports OSPF dynamic routing: configure router ospf, set router-id, define areas (backbone 0.0.0.0, stub, NSSA), add networks. OSPF updates routing table dynamically. Requires enabling OSPF on FortiGate interfaces
questions.explanation: FortiGate OSPF: config router ospf → set router-id → config area → config network (which subnets to advertise). Interface cost adjustable. Redistribute static/connected routes into OSPF. Supported: single-area, multi-area, stub/NSSA. ECMP supported. CLI or GUI configuration.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's two-factor authentication (2FA) for administrator login?
options: Adds a second verification factor to admin login: FortiToken (hardware or mobile TOTP app), email OTP, or SMS. Even if password is compromised, attacker needs the second factor. Configured per administrator account
questions.explanation: Admin 2FA: assign FortiToken to admin account. FortiToken Mobile: free app (TOTP). Hardware token: physical device. Email token: OTP sent to email. After password entry, 6-digit token required. Can also integrate with RADIUS/LDAP MFA servers. Critical for admin access security.

questions.question: How does FortiGate BGP support work?
options: FortiGate supports iBGP and eBGP routing — configure AS number, neighbor IP, and network advertisements. Used for: internet routing (multiple ISP), SD-WAN overlay routing, large enterprise networks. Advanced features: route maps, prefix lists, communities
questions.explanation: FortiGate BGP: config router bgp → set as (AS number) → config neighbor (peer IP, remote-as) → config network (advertise). Route maps/prefix lists for policy-based routing. eBGP multihop for non-directly-connected peers. Used with SD-WAN for overlay network routing.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's DNS filter?
options: Inspects DNS queries and responses — blocks resolution of domains categorized as malicious (botnet C&C, phishing, malware distribution) using FortiGuard DNS database before the connection even establishes. Complements web filtering
questions.explanation: DNS filter: intercepts DNS queries. Checks against FortiGuard botnet domain list and DNS category database. Block before HTTP connection — more efficient than web filter (blocks at DNS resolution phase). Can also: allow/block specific FQDNs, redirect blocked domains to FortiGate block page IP.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Threat Feed (IOC feed)?
options: External threat intelligence feeds (IP/domain/URL lists) that FortiGate uses to dynamically block known malicious IPs or domains — updates automatically from FortiGuard or external STIX/TAXII feeds, applied in security profiles
questions.explanation: Threat feeds: Security Fabric → Threat Feeds. Define external IP/domain/URL feed (HTTP/HTTPS source). FortiGate polls periodically. Apply in: Address objects (IP feeds), Web filter (domain feeds). External feeds: MISP, commercial threat intel. FortiGuard IP reputation: built-in Fortinet threat feed.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SD-WAN (Software-Defined WAN)?
options: Intelligently routes traffic across multiple WAN links (MPLS, broadband, LTE) based on application performance requirements — monitors link health (latency, jitter, packet loss) and routes traffic to best-performing link per application
questions.explanation: SD-WAN: define members (WAN interfaces/tunnels), performance SLAs (probe servers, thresholds), rules (match traffic → route to best member per SLA). Use cases: active/active dual ISP, application-aware routing (VoIP to MPLS, web to broadband), WAN optimization. Replaces policy-based routing.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate diagnose command and when is it used?
options: CLI commands for real-time troubleshooting: diagnose debug flow (packet trace), diagnose sniffer packet (tcpdump-like), diagnose sys top (process CPU), diagnose netlink dumpif (interface stats). Not available in GUI
questions.explanation: Key diagnose commands: 'diagnose sniffer packet any filter count' (packet capture). 'diagnose debug flow' (trace policy matching). 'diagnose debug app ike -1' (VPN debug). 'diagnose sys session list' (session table). Always disable debug after use ('diagnose debug disable' or wait for auto-disable timeout).

questions.question: What is FortiGate's log management and where can logs be sent?
options: Logs can be sent to: FortiAnalyzer (recommended for long-term storage, reporting, correlation), FortiCloud (cloud-based log storage), syslog server (any SIEM), local disk (limited space, not for production). Log types: traffic, event, security, virus, IPS
questions.explanation: FortiGate log destinations: FortiAnalyzer (best for enterprise — search, reports, correlation), FortiCloud (Fortinet SaaS logging), Syslog (up to 3 servers, SIEM integration), local disk (limited, overwrites). Log levels: emergency→debug. Traffic logs: high volume, balance verbosity vs storage.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA)?
options: ZTNA enforces per-application access control based on continuous device posture and user identity — uses FortiClient EMS and FortiGate to grant access only to specific apps (not full network), with ongoing verification of device compliance
questions.explanation: FortiGate ZTNA: FortiClient establishes ZTNA tunnel to FortiGate. EMS provides device certificate (posture verified). FortiGate ZTNA proxy: proxies access to specific backend servers only. Each access: re-verify device posture + user identity. Unlike VPN: no full network access.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate policy lookup tool?
options: GUI and CLI tool to trace which firewall policy would match a specific packet — enter source/destination IP, port, and interface to see which policy matches and what actions apply. Essential for troubleshooting traffic blocked or unexpectedly allowed
questions.explanation: Policy lookup: GUI → Policy & Objects → Firewall Policy → Policy Lookup. Specify: incoming interface, outgoing interface, protocol, source IP, destination IP, port. Shows which policy matches. Also: diagnose firewall iprope lookup (CLI). Useful for: verifying NAT, checking security profiles applied.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's DoS (Denial of Service) protection?
options: Separate from IPS — protects against volumetric attacks by rate-limiting or blocking traffic based on anomaly detection: SYN flood, UDP flood, ICMP flood, TCP port scan, UDP scan. Applied per interface, not per policy. Works at hardware level on supported models
questions.explanation: DoS policies: applied to physical interfaces (not firewall policies). Define anomaly thresholds: SYN/FIN/UDP/ICMP/TCP flood rates. Actions: block or pass. Monitored: per-source-IP or aggregate. Hardware-accelerated on NP platforms. Complements IPS (which handles exploits vs DoS handles volumetrics).

questions.question: What is FortiGate user authentication and captive portal?
options: FortiGate authenticates users via: local database, LDAP/AD (FSSO agent or LDAP query), RADIUS, SAML. Firewall policies can require authentication. Captive portal: force web browser authentication before granting internet access (common for guest WiFi)
questions.explanation: FSSO (Fortinet Single Sign-On): monitors AD logon events via DC agent or collector agent, associates IPs with users. Group-based policies: show/allow/deny based on AD group. Captive portal: HTTP redirect to login page. 802.1X: authenticate before switch port allowed. FortiAuthenticator: dedicated authentication server.

questions.question: What is FortiAnalyzer and what does it add over FortiGate local logging?
options: A dedicated Fortinet log management and analytics appliance/VM that centralizes logs from multiple FortiGates — provides: long-term log storage, advanced correlation, pre-built security reports, NOC/SOC dashboards, incident management, and FortiView analytics
questions.explanation: FortiAnalyzer: stores logs in compressed format, SQL-queryable. ADOMs (Administrative Domains): separate tenant data. Reports: compliance (PCI, HIPAA), traffic analysis, threat reports. FortiView: real-time and historical traffic views. Event correlation: multiple log events → security incident. Complementary product to FortiGate.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate ISDB (Internet Service Database)?
options: A built-in Fortinet database of IP ranges, ASNs, and port information for major internet services (Office 365, AWS, Google, Netflix, etc.) — use as source/destination in firewall policies to simplify rules for cloud services that use dynamic IP ranges
questions.explanation: ISDB: automatically updated by FortiGuard. Covers thousands of services with their IP ranges and expected ports. Use in policies: destination = 'Internet Service: Microsoft Office 365'. Eliminates manually tracking changing cloud service IP ranges. Also used in SD-WAN rules to steer specific service traffic.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's IKE (Internet Key Exchange) for IPsec VPN?
options: The key negotiation protocol for IPsec VPNs — IKEv1 (Phase 1: authentication/key material, Phase 2: tunnel parameters) and IKEv2 (simplified, faster, more secure). FortiGate supports both. IKEv2 recommended for new deployments
questions.explanation: IKEv1: Phase1 (Main/Aggressive mode) + Phase2 (Quick mode). IKEv2: single exchange, supports MOBIKE (mobile VPN), more efficient. Both: pre-shared key (PSK) or certificate authentication. DH groups: 14+ recommended (2048-bit). Encryption: AES-256. Hash: SHA-256+.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Botnet C&C protection?
options: Blocks communications to known botnet command-and-control servers — uses FortiGuard Botnet IP list to block outbound connections from compromised internal hosts to C&C infrastructure, detecting infected machines
questions.explanation: Botnet C&C detection: IP-based (blocked by FortiGuard IP reputation in IPS profile) and DNS-based (blocked by DNS filter). When internal host attempts to reach known C&C IP/domain, connection blocked and alert generated. Helps identify compromised machines on the network.

questions.question: What are FortiGate NP (Network Processor) and CP (Content Processor) ASICs?
options: NP ASICs: hardware accelerate firewall policy lookups, session setup, and encrypted VPN traffic — offload from main CPU. CP ASICs: accelerate content inspection (IPS, AV, SSL). Enable FortiGate to achieve high throughput while running security features
questions.explanation: FortiGate performance: NP ASICs (NP6, NP7) handle firewall/routing/VPN at wire speed without CPU involvement. CP ASICs (CP9) accelerate signature matching for IPS/AV. This is why FortiGate specs show different NGFW throughput (with CP) vs firewall throughput (NP accelerated). Higher model = more ASICs.

questions.question: What is the FortiGate packet flow order for processing traffic?
options: Ingress → DoS policy → Routing → Firewall policy (DNAT/VIP lookup first for inbound) → Security profiles (UTM) → Session table → Egress. Understanding this helps troubleshoot why traffic is blocked or inspected incorrectly
questions.explanation: Simplified FortiGate packet flow: (1) Ingress interface, (2) DoS policies, (3) Route lookup, (4) Session check (existing session), (5) Policy lookup (new session), (6) DNAT for inbound, (7) User authentication, (8) Security profiles, (9) SNAT, (10) Egress. VIP lookup happens before policy matching for inbound.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's Security Rating?
options: A continuous security posture assessment built into FortiGate/FortiManager that checks configuration against security best practices and assigns a score — identifies misconfigurations, unused features, and security gaps with remediation guidance
questions.explanation: Security Rating: checks FortiGate config against Fortinet best practices. Categories: security controls, fabric coverage, optimization. Score 0-100+. Shows specific issues: admin accounts without 2FA, weak cipher suites, unused security profiles, DNS filtering not enabled. Access: Security Fabric → Security Rating.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's inspection mode NGFW Policy Mode vs Profile-based Mode?
options: Profile-based (traditional): security profiles attached to individual policies. NGFW Policy Mode: application and URL categories used directly as policy match criteria (like PAN-OS), no separate security profiles — simpler for app-centric policies
questions.explanation: Profile-based: flexible, mature, most-used. Security profiles applied per-policy. NGFW Policy Mode: policies match on application/URL category directly. No separate AV/IPS profiles (configured globally). Simpler for application-centric security policies. Cannot mix modes per-VDOM. New in FortiOS 6.0+.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's SSL certificate inspection vs deep inspection?
options: Certificate inspection: checks certificate validity only (expired, revoked, untrusted CA) without decrypting content — no content inspection. Deep inspection: full decrypt, inspect, re-encrypt — requires pushing FortiGate CA to clients. Certificate inspection: less invasive, no content AV/IPS
questions.explanation: Choose based on requirements: Certificate inspection for compliance constraints (legal/privacy) or when distributing CA is impractical. Deep inspection when you need content inspection (AV, IPS, DLP, web filter) on HTTPS traffic — most corporate environments. Personal devices may reject deep inspection CA.

questions.question: What is FortiOS CLI configuration backup and restore?
options: Backup config: execute backup config {tftp|usb|ftp} FILENAME. Full config saved as text file (.conf). Restore: execute restore config. Partial restore: use CLI to paste specific sections. Automatic backup to FortiCloud/FortiManager recommended
questions.explanation: CLI backup: execute backup config tftp filename server-ip. Config file: human-readable text, contains all settings. Restore: execute restore config tftp filename server-ip (reboots to apply). Best practice: backup before changes, store off-device. FortiManager: centralized config backup for all managed FortiGates.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's URL filtering and what is a custom URL category?
options: URL filtering uses FortiGuard categories (75+ built-in) plus administrator-defined custom categories with specific URLs/wildcards — custom categories override FortiGuard classification for corporate exceptions or additional blocking requirements
URL filtering requires proxy mode only
URL filtering only works with SSL inspection
questions.explanation: URL filter: allow/block/monitor by FortiGuard category, custom URL list (exact/regex/wildcard), or custom category. Web rating override: temporarily change a URL's category. Local URL list evaluated before FortiGuard cloud lookup. Custom URLs: useful for business-specific allow/block lists.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's email filtering and spam protection?
options: FortiGate email filter inspects SMTP/IMAP/POP3 traffic for spam, phishing, malware attachments — uses FortiGuard Antispam service (IP reputation, email checksum, URL scanning in body), DNSBL checks, and heuristic analysis
questions.explanation: Email filter profile: apply to policies handling email traffic. Checks: FortiGuard antispam (cloud lookup), DNSBL/SURBL (DNS blacklist), content analysis, banned word lists. Actions: tag as spam, redirect to quarantine, discard. FortiMail: dedicated email security gateway — better for high-volume email environments.

questions.question: What is a FortiGate interface zone?
options: A logical grouping of FortiGate interfaces that can be referenced as a single object in firewall policies — simplifies policy management when multiple interfaces share the same trust level (e.g., all LAN ports in 'LAN zone')
questions.explanation: Zones: group interfaces of the same trust level. Policies reference zones instead of individual interfaces — reduces policy count. Intra-zone traffic: allow or block configurable. Interface can belong to only one zone. Common setup: LAN zone (internal ports), WAN zone (ISP interfaces), DMZ zone.

questions.question: What is the difference between FortiGate transparent mode and NAT mode?
options: NAT mode: FortiGate has IP addresses on interfaces and performs routing/NAT — acts as a router. Transparent mode: FortiGate operates as a Layer 2 bridge with no IP addresses on data interfaces — inserted into existing network without IP changes
questions.explanation: NAT mode: default, most common. Acts as gateway/router. Transparent mode: Bridge mode — useful for inserting security without changing IP addressing. Management IP still required for transparent mode admin. Useful for: inserting FortiGate between existing router and LAN without renumbering.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's FortiView?
options: Built-in traffic analytics tool that provides real-time and historical views of: top sources/destinations, applications, threats, web sites, cloud applications — helps identify traffic patterns, bandwidth hogs, and security events without needing FortiAnalyzer
questions.explanation: FortiView: built into FortiGate GUI. Real-time view: current session data. Historical view: last 1-24 hours (requires local disk or FortiAnalyzer). Drill-down: click on any source/app to see details. Top views: Applications, Cloud Apps, Sources, Destinations, Countries, Threats. Export to PDF/CSV.

questions.question: What are FortiGate route-based vs policy-based IPsec VPNs?
options: Route-based: creates a virtual IPsec interface — traffic routed to tunnel via routing table. More flexible, supports dynamic routing (BGP/OSPF), preferred for most deployments. Policy-based: traffic matching a specific policy encrypted — older, simpler, less flexible
questions.explanation: Route-based VPN: virtual tunnel interface created. Add routes pointing through tunnel interface. Supports dynamic routing. Easier to troubleshoot (use routing table). Recommended for all new deployments. Policy-based: match-based encryption, no tunnel interface — harder to route, can't do dynamic routing. Legacy method.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's built-in sandbox integration (FortiSandbox)?
options: Submits suspicious files to FortiSandbox (physical, VM, or cloud) for dynamic execution analysis — detonates files in isolated environment to detect zero-day malware that evades signature-based detection. Results feed back to FortiGuard threat intelligence
questions.explanation: FortiSandbox integration: FortiGate AV profile → enable 'send to FortiSandbox'. Unknown files: hold (block until result) or pass (allow while scanning). FortiSandbox analyzes in VM, provides verdict. Positive verdict → FortiGuard global block. Cloud sandbox: FortiCloud Sandbox (subscription). Inline blocking optional.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's local-in policy?
options: Controls traffic destined for the FortiGate itself (not traffic passing through) — limits which IPs can access management services (HTTPS, SSH, SNMP, BGP). More granular than trusted hosts in admin accounts. Applied to management plane traffic
questions.explanation: Local-in policies: protect FortiGate management. Example: only allow HTTPS management from management VLAN, block all others. Overrides 'allow access' settings on interfaces. Use when multiple interfaces have HTTPS admin enabled but you want granular control per source IP. CLI: config firewall local-in-policy.

questions.question: What is FortiGate 802.1X authentication for wired networks?
options: Port-based network access control using 802.1X — FortiGate as RADIUS server or proxy to authenticate users/devices connecting to FortiSwitch ports before granting network access. Validates credentials via AD/LDAP, assigns VLAN dynamically based on user group
questions.explanation: 802.1X on FortiGate+FortiSwitch: define RADIUS server profile, enable 802.1X on switch ports. Authentication: EAP-TLS (certificates), EAP-PEAP (password). Dynamic VLAN assignment: RADIUS returns VLAN-ID, switch puts port in correct VLAN. Guest VLAN for failed authentication. FortiNAC: full NAC solution.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's consolidated policy table?
options: A unified view in FortiGate GUI showing all policy types (firewall, NAT, authentication, traffic shaping) in one table — available in FortiOS 7.0+. Enables seeing all policies that affect traffic in one place
questions.explanation: Consolidated policy view (FortiOS 7.0+): single table shows IPv4/IPv6 policies, authentication rules, traffic shaping policies. Filter and search across all. Reduces need to navigate multiple menus. Optional view — can still use separate tables. Helps with policy auditing.

questions.question: What is FortiGate's antivirus grayware detection?
options: Detects potentially unwanted applications (PUAs/PUPs): adware, riskware, spyware, dialers — not strictly malware but potentially harmful or unwanted. Separate from malware detection, configurable to block or just monitor
questions.explanation: Grayware: legitimately available software that may be used maliciously (keyloggers, remote admin tools, adware). FortiGate AV profile: enable Grayware detection. Actions: monitor (log only) or block. Helps detect dual-use tools (legitimate admin tools used by attackers) in corporate environments.

questions.question: What is FortiManager and how does it differ from vCenter for VMware?
options: FortiManager: centralized management platform for multiple FortiGate devices — manages policies, firmware upgrades, configurations, and provides a centralized database of objects. Similar concept to vCenter but for FortiGate firewalls instead of ESXi hosts
questions.explanation: FortiManager: manages multiple FortiGates. ADOMs (Admin Domains): group devices by customer/region. Policy packages: create once, push to multiple FortiGates. Object database: shared addresses, services, schedules. Firmware management: stage and deploy across fleet. API for automation. Complementary to FortiAnalyzer (logging).
